$comment: Read by scripts/harvest-cropontology.mjs and scripts/build.mjs. `include` is a regex on ontologyDbId; only matching ontologies are harvested and published. Display names are the upstream ontologyName with `stripWords` removed (whole words, case-insensitive), unless `names` overrides them by id. The original name is kept in additionalInfo.sourceOntologyName. `planteomePaths` lists extra files (repo-relative) to copy from a Planteome repo when its trait data is not at the root; `planteomeFiles` picks the file to compare when a repo has several. `siteReloadsCountFrom`: cropontology.org reloads before this date (its 2023 migration re-imported old content) do not count as newer than GitHub. `traitClasses` standardises trait class names. `textRepairs` restores characters a source lost. `sources` forces which copy wins when the two disagree.

traitClasses.$comment: Trait class names are standardised so one class isn't listed under several spellings (e.g. wheat's "Phenological traits" and "Phenological"). Each part of a class ("Quality/Aroma" has two) that matches an `aliases` key or a `standard` class, ignoring case and a trailing "trait" or "traits", is spelled as the alias target or standard class; every part then starts with a capital letter. `regroup` then moves a crop's one-off classes into the common ones, by ontology ID and the class name as spelled after those rules (keys match case-insensitively); quality-type classes keep their original name as a subclass ("Quality/Viscosity"). A class whose subclass is itself a `standard` class becomes that class ("Agronomic/Postharvest" becomes "Postharvest"). Last, a British spelling in `americanSpellings` becomes the American one when more of the class's trait names use the American spelling (sweet potato's odor traits give "Quality/Odor"). Finally a class with a subclass is served as its parent class, with the subclass in the trait's additionalInfo.traitSubclass ("Quality/Odor" is served as "Quality", subclass "Odor"), so each crop lists only a few classes. The source value is kept in the trait's additionalInfo.sourceTraitClass.

textRepairs.$comment: Characters a source stored as "?" (lost when the text was uploaded) or garbled, restored from context. Per ontology ("*" applies to all), each `find` is a regular expression applied in order to every text field of every variable and replaced by `replace` (which may use $1 for a captured group); `only` limits a repair to the listed variables; `why` says what was lost. Repairs are listed on the Conflicts page with the other text repairs.
